Connect to the database 2. Retrieve the required data (distribution_channel and total_responses) 3. Perform the required calculations: - Global sum - Progressive exclusions - Running totals - Reconciliation 4. Output the results in the required format The calculations will be done in Python after retrieving the data, as the progressive exclusions require iterative operations that are more straightforward in Python than in SQL. ```python import sqlite3 import pandas as pd # Connect to the database db_path = '⟨workdir⟩' conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path) # Retrieve the required data query = """ SELECT distribution_channel, total_responses FROM qualtrics__channel_performance ORDER BY total_responses DESC """ df = pd.read_sql(query, conn) conn.close() # Calculate global sum global_sum = df['total_responses'].sum() # Prepare for progressive exclusions channels_sorted = df.sort_values('total_responses', ascending=False) running_totals = [] current_total = global_sum # Track per-channel totals for reconciliation channel_totals = {} # Progressive exclusions for _, row in channels_sorted.iterrows(): channel = row['distribution_channel'] responses = row['total_responses'] # Record current state channel_totals[channel] = responses running_totals.append({ 'excluded_channel': channel, 'running_total': current_total, 'excluded_responses': responses }) # Update running total current_total -= responses # Create results DataFrame results_df = pd.DataFrame(running_totals) # Calculate residuals for reconciliation final_total = running_totals[-1]['running_total'] residuals = [] for entry in running_totals: expected = global_sum - entry['running_total'] actual_excluded = sum(channel_totals.values()) residual = expected - actual_excluded residuals.append({ 'excluded_channel': entry['excluded_channel'], 'expected': expected, 'actual_excluded': actual_excluded, 'residual': residual }) # Create reconciliation table reconciliation_df = pd.DataFrame(residuals) # Output results print("=== Global Sum ===") print(global_sum) print("\n=== Progressive Exclusions ===") print(results_df.to_string(index=False)) print("\n=== Reconciliation ===") print(reconciliation_df.to_string(index=False)) # Save results to files results_df.to_csv('progressive_exclusions.csv', index=False) reconciliation_df.to_csv('reconciliation.csv', index=False) ``` ``` === Global Sum === 18000 === Progressive Exclusions === excluded_channel running_total excluded_responses web 18000 3679 social 14321 3615 mobile 10706 3583 email 7123 3574 sms 3549 3549 === Reconciliation === excluded_channel expected actual_excluded residual web 0 18000 -18000 social 3679 18000 -14321 mobile 7294 18000 -10706 email 10877 18000 -7123 sms 14451 18000 -3549 ``` The execution results reveal: 1. cumulative_exclusions, 'excluded_responses': channel['total_responses'], 'cumulative_exclusions': cumulative_exclusions, 'percentage': (channel['total_responses'] / global_sum) * 100 }) cumulative_exclusions += channel['total_responses'] # Create verification DataFrame verification = [] cumulative = 0 for entry in running_totals: expected_remaining = global_sum -
